purpose: Replace mistaken dolphin identity with existing gray shark; rebuild original mouth anatomy.

arguments.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw Image 1, the exact original SLEVEJM2 002 sprite, as one polished cartoon SHARK sprite. Image 1 controls pose, mouth shape, facing, visible anatomy, framing and water occlusion. Images 2 and 3 are CHARACTER DESIGN AND DRAWING STYLE ONLY, not pose. Match the established shark: neutral medium gray skin, pale ivory jaw and underside, gill slits, bold black outlines, smooth restrained cel shading, heavy sly brows and razor-sharp triangular teeth. This is the sneaky shark character, never a friendly dolphin; no dolphin beak or rounded dolphin teeth. Pose: Tall upright right-facing shark in rear three-quarter view. Gray back/flank dominates, pale belly only a narrow strip at right. The compact upper head tilts upward, while the original's large open mouth has a tooth-filled opening and a projecting lower jaw lifted toward upper-right with a blunt end. Small sly eye belongs HIGH ON THE UPPER HEAD; the black-white patch below it is the open toothy mouth. Backward dorsal fin extends to lower-left; near pectoral fin hangs against the flank. Preserve the jaw angle, tall upright silhouette, and water occlusion. Preserve the source silhouette and relative positions while replacing pixel steps with smooth ink. Only the character parts above water are drawn, with a thin cyan-and-white ripple at original cutoff. Do not complete submerged body, tail or legs. One character only. All contours inside canvas with clear transparent padding on every edge. Actual transparent RGBA background, no checkerboard, scene, cast shadow, glow, text or collage.
